reading: The input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3). The output is a fixed 3x3 pattern in colour 8 chosen by that dominant colour: 1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080.

slots.feature: most frequent non-background colour of the input

why: every pair's output is the pattern listed for its majority colour

reading: Each isolated marker cell gets a 3x3 ring around it (marker kept in the centre). The ring colour depends on the marker colour: 3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1.
why: every marker's 8 neighbours become key(marker colour); all other cells unchanged

reading: The 3x3 input is copied into an n x n grid of 3x3 blocks, where n is the number of background cells; the number of copies equals the number of non-background cells, laid out in reading order from the top-left, the rest of the blocks empty.
why: each output block is the input or empty; #copies = #fg cells, blocks per side = #bg cells, copies fill row-major
invariants: each non-empty block equals the input exactly

reading: Every input cell is scaled up into a 3x3 block of its colour (3x3 -> 9x9).

slots.subject: whole input, each cell -> factor x factor block of its own colour

why: output cell (y,x) equals input cell (y//3, x//3)

reading: Four colour-5 markers (top, bottom, left, right) bound a box; a rectangle outline in the colour of the small hollow shape is drawn one cell inside the markers, i.e. on rows top+1 and bottom-1 and columns left+1 and right-1.

slots.bounds: the four markers (min row, max row, min col, max col of the 5-cells)

why: the only changed cells are the outline of the rectangle [top+1..bottom-1] x [left+1..right-1], painted in the shape's colour
invariants: markers and the original shape stay

reading: The grid is divided into equal cells by full separator lines; one cell holds a small pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose row index and column index differ from the pattern cell's by an even number (every second cell in both directions).

slots.unit: contents of the one non-empty panel cell
slots.anchors: panel cells at cell-offsets (2i, 2j) from the pattern cell
slots.colour: new pattern colour as in the source

why: a panel cell holds the pattern iff its (row, col) cell index has the same parity as the source cell; all other cells stay empty

reading: The top row (above a separator line of 5) is a colour key c0,c1,c2,...; around the single marker below, concentric square rings are drawn: the centre keeps c0, ring k (Chebyshev distance k) gets colour ck, for as many key entries as given (0 entries leave a background ring).

slots.key: the colour sequence in row 0 left to right, up to the last non-zero entry
slots.anchor: the single marker cell below the separator (equals key[0])
slots.rule: cells at Chebyshev distance k from the anchor get key[k]

why: every cell within distance len(key)-1 of the marker has colour key[distance]; cells farther away unchanged
invariants: key row unchanged (pair 0 alters one key cell 8 -> 5, an apparent quirk)

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is painted (clipped to the grid) in the colour of the block cell diagonally opposite that corner.

slots.subject: the 2x2 four-colour block
slots.anchors: the four 2x2 areas diagonally adjacent to the block's corners
slots.colour: colour of the block cell opposite the corner (top-left area gets bottom-right colour, etc.)

why: each corner 2x2 area is filled with the colour of the diagonally opposite block cell; the block itself unchanged

reading: Rectangular frames are marked by four L-shaped corner brackets; the colour-1 pattern inside each frame occupies one half and is mirrored across the frame's centre line (perpendicular to its long side) so the interior becomes symmetric. Stray colour-1 cells outside any frame are erased.

slots.parts: each frame delimited by four corner brackets
slots.axis: the frame's middle line across its longer dimension
slots.subject: colour-1 cells inside the frame, reflected and unioned with the original
slots.outside: colour-1 cells not inside any frame are cleared

why: inside every frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's midline and contains the original; no 1-cells remain outside frames

reading: Full lines of 5 cut the grid into panels; the top-left panel is filled with 1, the centre panel (middle row band, middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right panel with 3.

slots.parts: panels cut by full separator rows and columns
slots.targets: top-left panel -> 1, centre panel -> 2, bottom-right panel -> 3 (train constants)

why: only those three panels change, each filled entirely with its constant colour
